scoring: Each criterion is pass (1), partial (0.5) or fail (0). A region's score is 10 x its credited fraction, rounded to 0.1. Measured criteria are computed by loop_tools.py into the packet's measured.json and are copied, never re-judged. Visual criteria are judged by the critic from the named images.

R01.text: Front head band silhouette overlaps the first sheet: IoU at least .90
Side head band silhouette overlaps the first sheet: IoU at least .90
A round skull crown rises between the ear roots in the front view instead of sitting level with the inner fan rim

From behind, a rounded head mass reads centred in the fan and meets it through a soft concave valley, with no convex rim, ridge, seam or separate disc (reworded 2026-10-01: "blends into it" led builders to blur the head into a bowl)
The lower face tapers to a small rounded chin (a soft U), with no square jaw and no pinched stem
Back view width at .18 of figure height (the head base inside the fan) at most 1.15x the sheet
Side view head depth at .22 at most 1.15x the sheet

Gestalt (added 2026-09-30 from gap-audit-0226.md): in the back view a round head mass reads in the centre of the fan as its own dome, narrower than the wings, with the neck tapering out of its bottom; fails when the centre of the back view is one continuous surface from tip to tip

R02.text: The eyes are very large tall ovals set into shallow sockets; in profile the eye is no prouder than the brow and cheek

The eye outline is a bold dark outline all the way around the eye, as the eye reference r01 draws it, carried by darkness and set flush into the face, not a raised tube or a disc standing proud (Nick 2026-10-07: bold outline, replacing "a thin lid line, not a thick raised black ring")
A small dark triangular nose pad sits seated in the muzzle, not a flat tab or a stuck-on bead
The muzzle is one soft rounded mass with a closed w mouth, no knob under the mouth, and in profile it stays behind the nose tip
Soft cheek tufts break the lower face outline as broad coat masses, not jagged plates and not invisible relief

Gestalt (added 2026-09-30 from gap-audit-0226.md; ring clause removed 2026-10-07 by Nick's bold-outline ruling): in true profile the brow and the nose tip both stand in front of the eye surface; fails on a disc eye at the front line

R03.text: Front ear span within 3 percent of the first sheet
Front head band: at most 6 percent of the reference fan area is left uncovered
The fan outline has the V tilt of the first sheet: crown about .02 to .03 of figure height below the tips, and each tip tapers to an up-flared point, not a blunt square end
The fan front is built from large shaggy pointed locks radiating from the ear roots (roughly 8 to 10 per side), not knobs, thorns, scales, shingles or lumps
A cupped inner ear reads from the front on each side: a real hollow beside the skull with a clean rim and a pointed upper tip
The lower fan edge drapes toward the cheeks instead of lifting clear of them

Gestalt (added 2026-09-30 from gap-audit-0226.md): each ear cup is filled by a pale, fluffy, pointed inner tuft covering at least half of the cup in the front view, and the fan edge is a run of pointed locks with no crinkled rim, thorn or flat leaf plane anywhere

R04.text: Back head band silhouette overlaps the first sheet: IoU at least .90
Side head band: model-only area at most 6 percent of the reference
From behind, the fan is one soft shaggy mass whose locks flow down and outward from a crown tuft, with no bowl rim, lattice, tiles, teeth or seams
The top edge rises spiky toward the tips and domes toward the crown; from above and behind it does not read as a flat tray
In profile the fan sweeps up and back as a curved shell of locks around a visible cavity, with no slabs, pins, picket or seam
Back view width at .20 at most 1.15x the sheet

Gestalt (added 2026-09-30 from gap-audit-0226.md): in the back and rear oblique views the fan's back is covered in down-and-outward locks with no smooth area larger than one lock, and nothing reads as a bowl, cup, basin rim or mushroom

R05.text: Front neck width within 10 percent of the first sheet
Side neck depth within 15 percent of the first sheet
Front shoulder width within 7 percent of the first sheet
The head meets the neck in a soft furred transition under the jaw and at the nape, with no stem pinch, notch or kink
The shoulders slope down from the neck to soft rounded caps, with no square yoke, corner nubs, ledges or bands

Gestalt (added 2026-09-30 from gap-audit-0226.md): the arm leaves the trunk from a rounded shoulder cap at the top corner of the trunk, not from the side of a sloping web, and from behind there is no collar ring, disc or ledge on the neck or across the shoulders

R06.text: Front waist at most 10 percent wider than the first sheet
The trunk tapers smoothly from rib cage to waist to hips, with no shelf or abrupt flare
The chest has a soft forward plane and rib cage volume, not a smooth tube
The figure reads slim, not athletic, with a restrained rear
Side view: the chest front at .36 stands ahead of the chin front at .22 as in the sheet, within .01 of figure height

Gestalt (added 2026-09-30 from gap-audit-0226.md): in the side view the trunk visibly narrows from rib cage to waist and fills out again at the rump, and no horizontal crease or belt line crosses the belly, flank or back
Posed to the sheet (hands on hips), tail-free halves, mean of front, left and back: trunk band IoU at least .90
Trunk side depth over the upper chest (mean of .32 and .34, mesh section, arms excluded) within .97 to 1.10 of the sheet's trunk depth there (.125 of figure height)
Trunk side depth at the waist (smallest of .42, .44 and .46, mesh section) within .95 to 1.08 of the sheet's trunk depth (.0816 of figure height), no wasp waist and no plank
Trunk chest depth (deeper of .34 and .36) over trunk waist depth (smallest of .42 to .46) within .93 to 1.08 of the sheet's ratio (1.60), the rib cage clearly deeper than the waist
Dorsal S curve, upper half: the trunk's back edge swings forward from the rib cage (.34) to the lumbar hollow (.44) by at least .9 of the sheet's swing (.052 of figure height)

Belly front line: the trunk's front edge from .40 to .48 departs from the straight line between .38 and .50 by no more than .004 of figure height more than the sheet's does (no pouch, no band, no pigeon breast)

R07.text: The upper arm is round in cross-section with no flat facet or hard-edged slab
The arm has a readable elbow and a wrist narrower than the forearm
Each forepaw has four digit lobes, each with a short curved claw coming out of its tip
The forepaw is a compact animal paw with no human fingers or thumb, palm toward the thigh

Gestalt (added 2026-09-30 from gap-audit-0226.md): in the front view each forepaw ends in a blunt rounded paw at least as wide as the wrist with claws visible at the tip; nothing about it reads as a single finger, thumb or bud
Posed to the sheet (hands on hips), tail-free halves, mean of front, left and back: arm band IoU at least .90 (upper arm and forearm lengths and thickness)

R08.text: Each lower leg has one smooth calf swell, with no double bulge and no low shin lump
The knee reads as a soft kneecap plane, not a knob or a groove
The thighs are strong and full but not rabbit-like
The ankles and heels taper; they are not thick
Front ankle width (narrowest from .86 to .94) at most 1.15x the sheet
Back ankle width (narrowest from .86 to .94) at most 1.15x the sheet
Front shin width at .85 at most 1.1x the sheet
Front ankle over thigh (.68) at most 1.2x the sheet's ratio: the leg tapers to a slim ankle

Gestalt (added 2026-09-30 from gap-audit-0226.md): in the front and back views the ankle is plainly the thinnest point of the leg, under half the thigh, and the outline between knee and ankle has exactly one gentle swell; fails on a column leg or a wavy outline

Posed to the sheet (hands on hips), tail-free halves, mean of front, left and back: thigh band IoU at least .85 (the sheet places the leg about .03 apart between its front and back figures, so one 3D leg tops out near .85 to .90; R08 spec, 2026-10-01)
Posed to the sheet (hands on hips), tail-free halves, mean of front, left and back: shin band IoU at least .72 (same sheet inconsistency; an exact-spec leg reaches about .71 unshifted)

R09.text: The toe row arches: the middle toes lead and the outer toes are smaller, not four equal beads in a straight row
Short claws emerge from the toe tips and curve down, not spikes standing clear
The paw has a heel, a sloping top and a flat sole in full ground contact
The paw size reads right against the leg, as in the paw study
Back view paw width (widest from .96 to .99) over ankle width at least .8 of the sheet's ratio: the paw is a broad fan well wider than the ankle

Back view paw width at .96 at least .85 of the sheet (replaces the side instep row, which read two staggered sheet paws as one; R09 spec, 2026-10-01). R09.6 side paw length was dropped for the same reason.

Gestalt (added 2026-09-30 from gap-audit-0226.md): in the front view each hind paw is a broad rounded fan of large toe lobes, clearly wider than the ankle, middle toes leading, with long curved claws coming out of the toe tips; in the side view the toes rise into a domed instep
Posed to the sheet (hands on hips), tail-free halves, mean of front, left and back: foot band IoU at least .85

R10.text: Back view against the accepted back study, trunk band (upper tails): IoU at least .74
Back view against the accepted back study, legs band (lower tails): IoU at least .72
Each tail is a full crescent whose tip curls up and out, as in the back study, not a leaf or a downward hook
The tails lie shingled in a stack on one side, overlapping near the root, not splayed like fingers
Each tail is full near the root and tapers smoothly to a point; in profile the tails read as layered crescents, not pods

R11.text: The three tails fuse into one root at the base of the spine, centred on the sacrum, not on one hip
The root mass overlaps onto both rear sides
No crease, pinch or V fold where the root meets the body or where the tails part
The root reads as one sheath before the tails split

R12.text: Every part is at one level of development: body coat masses (cheek, chest, forearm or calf tufts) match the head fan's, or the fan is simplified to the body's level
One coat idiom is used across the model: fan front, fan rear and body masses read as the same kind of fur lock
No stray lumps, knots, seams, facets or placeholder shapes anywhere
Proportions read as one creature: head, fan, body and tails in the first sheet's balance

Gestalt (added 2026-09-30 from gap-audit-0226.md): shown model and sheet side by side at equal height, the same three words describe both bodies (the sheet: slim, lithe, long limbed); fails on stocky, toy, tube, ape or stalk
